newsitem.title: CANADA: Oil and gas drilling record set in Canada in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Oil and gas drilling record set in Canada in 1996.

text.p: Energy companies, buoyed by surging oil and gas prices, drilled a record 12,695 wells in Canada last year for the third straight annual well count over 10,000, an industry newsletter reported on Thursday.

Nickle's Daily Oil Bulletin, which tracks Canadian oil and gas statistics, said drilling in 1996 surpassed the previous high set in 1994, when 11,870 wells were drilled. In 1995, companies drilled 11,062 wells in Canada.
The publication said high crude prices meant a strong focus on oil drilling in Alberta and Saskatchewan.

In Alberta, 4,373 oil wells were drilled last year, a 17 percent jump over the previous high set in 1985. The industry drilled 1,838 oil wells in Saskatchewan, short of the record 2,816 tally set in 1985, the year before the infamous world oil price crash, the Bulletin said.

It said light crude oil prices at Edmonton for 1996 averaged C$29.37 per barrel, a 21 percent increase from the average of C$24.21 in 1995. Prices in December averaged C$33.62 per barrel, the highest monthly average in more than five years, the Bulletin said.
Spot natural gas prices at Alberta's AECO-C Hub averaged C$1.39 per gigajoule in 1996, 23 percent higher than the 1995 average of C$1.13 per gigajoule.
Spot gas at AECO was fetching over C$2 per gigajoule at the end of 1996.
The Bulletin said it predicted 10,500 wells would be drilled in Canada in 1997, a figure matching projections from other organizations such as the Petroleum Services Association of Canada.
